Build me a sparse, decaying industrial district at amber dusk, with deep blue-black shadows, hazy air, and a flat, largely featureless pale-beige ground plane stretching between isolated structures. Organize the scene around a broad elevated roadway running lengthwise through the district on regular concrete piers, its unusually bright, plain deck dominating the aerial views; place a narrower rusted steel rail viaduct diagonally across and beneath it, with exposed trusses and dark tracks. Cluster roughly twenty-five brick warehouses, workshops, and tenement-like blocks along both corridors, leaving broad empty lots and unfinished-looking gaps between them. Most buildings should be rectangular, two to four stories tall, with red or faded tan brick, weathered plaster patches, repetitive dark windows, flat or gently pitched rust-streaked roofs, and occasional decorative cornices; include several larger freestanding mill buildings around the outer area and smaller sheds packed near the central crossing. Add wooden utility poles and dense sagging overhead wires along the streets, chain-link fencing and graffiti-covered metal barriers beneath the viaduct, exterior fire escapes, narrow catwalks, suspended industrial pipes, rooftop vents, service doors, steps, and shadowed passages between buildings. Keep streets and yards empty of people and vehicles, with no vegetation and little visible surface detailing. Frame the distant edges with thin, hazy silhouettes of a modern city skyline, while keeping the reconstructed district low-rise, fragmented, and irregularly spaced, denser around the rail junction and markedly emptier toward the perimeter.
